classification.difficultyReason: Identify the internal radius as the triangle’s missing shorter side, use Pythagoras to find it, then calculate the quadrant arc and combine only the outer boundary lengths. These are routine linked procedures with a boundary interpretation and an exact-form answer.

content.prompt:
A shape consisting of a quadrant and a right-angled triangle is shown.
What is the perimeter, in exact form?

spec.sourceRegion: Q9 figure below the stem, left side
spec.description: Unshaded quadrant above a right-angled triangle. The vertical radius continues down to the triangle’s lower vertex. A dashed horizontal radius separates the quadrant and triangle. Matching single ticks mark the two radii, with a right-angle marker at their intersection. External dimension arrows label the lower vertical side 6 cm; the sloping triangle side is labelled 10 cm.
spec.mathematics: The right triangle has hypotenuse 10 cm and vertical leg 6 cm, so its horizontal leg and the quadrant radius are 8 cm. The exterior circular boundary is a 90-degree arc. The internal horizontal radius is excluded from the perimeter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens 6 cm and 10 cm appear; the radius, arc length and perimeter are withheld.

answer.worked:
Let $r$ be the quadrant radius and $L$ its arc length. A quadrant is one-quarter of a circle.
$$\begin{align*}r&=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8\ \text{cm}\\L&=\frac14\times2\pi\times8=4\pi\ \text{cm}\\P&=4\pi+8+6+10\\P&=(24+4\pi)\ \text{cm}\end{align*}$$
The dashed radius is internal, so it is excluded from the perimeter.
